subject: Re: CloudCorp RFP – benchmarking deep-dive and proposed joint test plan
messages:
From: Tom Ellis <t.ellis@cloudcorp.com>
To: rafael_mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: CloudCorp RFP <rfp@cloudcorp.com>
Date: Mon, 27 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: CloudCorp RFP - performance questionnaire follow-up

Rafael,

Thanks for the quick response last week. The procurement team has one remaining packet of detailed questions around performance and our benchmarking expectations before we move to commercial terms. We want to run a short joint benchmark (controlled) and also validate your published p95/p99 numbers under our workload profile. High level asks:

- Provide a test plan that covers latency (p50/p95/p99), throughput (QPS and tokens/sec), and steady-state vs burst scenarios.
- Describe warm-up and cache-warm strategies, and how you account for KV cache priming.
- Explain autoscaling/overprovision behavior under a spike (5x baseline for 60s).
- Share the hardware matrix you used for published numbers (GPU type, memory, quantization).
- Confirm any behavioral differences when you enable quantization or use smaller model variants.

Can you share a runnable test plan and, if possible, a proposed slot for a joint execution next week? We're aiming to close the technical validation by May 7.

--Tom
Tom Ellis
Sr. Sourcing Manager, CloudCorp
Tom.Ellis@cloudcorp.com

From: rafael_mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Tom Ellis <t.ellis@cloudcorp.com>
Cc: CloudCorp RFP <rfp@cloudcorp.com>, lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Apr 2026 08:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: CloudCorp RFP - performance questionnaire follow-up

Tom — thanks, we can absolutely do this. Attached is a concise joint-test plan (redwood_benchmarking_protocol_v1.pdf) and a CSV that maps the hardware/quantization matrix we used for our published figures. Summary below; details are in the attachment.

Quick summary (top-line):
- Measured metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency (in ms) per request, tokens/sec, system-level QPS (requests/sec), and GPU utilization. We also capture tail-latency percentiles for token-level stepping when streaming.
- Test profiles:
  1) Cold-start ramp (measured from cold process start; KV cache empty) — 3 runs; 10k requests each; 1s inter-request pause to isolate startup variance.
  2) Warm steady-state (KV cache primed) — sustained steady load for 30 minutes; target concurrency equal to production concurrency sample provided in your questionnaire.
  3) Burst resilience test — baseline steady-state, then 5x request spike for 60s followed by 10 minutes of recovery to observe autoscaling and throttling behavior.
  4) Token-heavy vs prompt-heavy profiles — separate runs where the average token-per-request is 32 vs 512 to highlight batching and KV-cache behavior.

- Warm-up/KV priming: We recommend a controlled KV priming pass (one-off sweep using a representative prefix set) prior to the warm steady-state window. We document exact priming workload and duration in the attachment.

- Autoscaling/fallback behavior: Redwood Dedicated will scale by adding replica capacity (horizontal) and expanding batching thresholds up to configured limits. For the joint run we will use a deterministic scaling policy that mirrors your on-prem requirements (we show expected provisioning latency and SLOs in the doc). If capacity is constrained, Redwood will automatically route to a compatible lower-cost model variant per your policy; we document expected p99 deltas.

- Hardware/quantization matrix (see CSV): published figures were gathered on A40-class GPUs and on 80GB A100 variants with int8 quantization path available for select models. The CSV enumerates model variants, seq length, batch sizes, and observed tokens/sec.

Next steps proposed:
- We can run a joint execution slot on Thursday 30 Apr 2026 at 10:00am PT (I attached a calendar invite). Can you confirm your test lead?
- We will provide remote access to a sandbox with pre-populated KV prefixes and a small dataset to mirror your privacy constraints.

Attachments: redwood_benchmarking_protocol_v1.pdf; redwood-inference-performance-matrix.csv

If you want a shorter executive summary to attach to the RFP, I can produce a one-pager.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

From: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: rafael_mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: grace_oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 29 Apr 2026 11:36:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: CloudCorp RFP - performance questionnaire follow-up

Quick edits to the draft reply:
- Add explicit note about network egress being excluded from our reported token/sec (CloudCorp asked earlier).
- Call out the warmup duration (we use 6 minutes of controlled priming) — that avoids ambiguous wording in the attachment.
- In the autoscaling paragraph, add a short sentence about our graceful-degradation policy: when replica scale-up is slower than the spike, we enforce per-route throttling with prioritized fallbacks to cached responses.

Two minor asks for the joint run:
1) Can you confirm whether CloudCorp wants TLS mutual auth for the sandbox? If yes, we need cert exchange by EOD Wed.
2) Please add a short note to the calendar invite that the test will be recorded for post-run analysis.

I'll attach a redline of the PDF; Rafael, please send once updated.

- Lauren
Director, Solutions Engineering
lauren.bishop@redwood.com

From: rafael_mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Tom Ellis <t.ellis@cloudcorp.com>
Cc: CloudCorp RFP <rfp@cloudcorp.com>, lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, grace_oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2026 17:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: CloudCorp RFP - performance questionnaire follow-up

Tom — thanks for the patience. Attached are the updated protocol and the hardware/quantization matrix. Changes from the draft: network egress is excluded from tokens/sec; warmup priming is specified as 6 minutes; and we added the graceful-degradation paragraph per Lauren's suggestion.

We confirmed the joint execution slot for Thu, 30 Apr 2026 10:00am PT (attached .ics). For the sandbox connection: we support mTLS and are prepared to exchange certs — please send CloudCorp's test cert to rafael.mendes@redwood.com by EOD Wed so we can pre-stage.

Run plan highlights (what we'll measure live):
- Baseline steady-state at your stated concurrency, 30-minute window.
- Burst: 5x instantaneous increase sustained for 60s. We will capture autoscaler reaction time, queue depth, request drop rate (if any), and p99 before/during/after the spike.
- Token distribution runs: short (32 tokens) and long (512 tokens) to show batching/throughput differences.
- Long-tail token stepping: for streaming responses, we'll capture per-token latencies for the first 128 tokens to illustrate token-stepping behavior and tail amplification.

What you'll get after the run:
- Raw logs (sanitized), aggregated latency/throughput CSVs, GPU utilization and scheduler traces, and a short write-up with recommended tuning changes (batch size, quantization recommendation, and autoscaler thresholds).

Links and references:
- HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.example/record/CC-2026-019
- Shared sandbox folder (drive): https://drive.example.com/drive/folders/benchmarking-sandbox

Please confirm the test lead and whether you will send the certs for mTLS. If you'd prefer to move the run to Friday morning instead, we have a flexible slot.

Best regards,
Rafael Mendes
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: redwood_benchmarking_protocol_v1.pdf; cloudcorp_joint-test-schedule.ics; redwood-inference-performance-matrix.csv
